summary:
# NOTES: "Dr. Rumsey's Patient: A Very Strange Story" (1896)
Authors: L. T. Meade and Dr. Halifax (Clifford Halifax). Hurst & Co., New York. One book, 24 chapters.

## Characters
- **Robert "Bob"/"Mr. Robert" Awdrey**: young Squire of The Court, Grandcourt, Wiltshire. Balliol, double first. Dark gray eyes. Turns 21 on Monday (Aug 22 implied, wedding "24th"). Later Dr. Rumsey's patient.
- **Margaret Douglas (later Mrs. Awdrey)**: Cuthbert cousin, tall, black eyes, raven hair, olive skin. Engaged to Awdrey at picnic. Son Arthur.
- **Hetty Armitage (later Hetty Vincent)**: niece of innkeeper Armitage, Red Doe Inn, Grandcourt. Beautiful, flirtatious, black curls. Secretly loves Awdrey. Witness; later kills husband with laudanum; dies after confession.
- **Horace Frere**: undergraduate, Balliol. Proposes to Hetty. Killed by Awdrey's stick in right eye on Salisbury Plain.
- **Frank Everett**: undergraduate, Balliol, friend of Frere. Square-built, handsome. Wrongly convicted; 14 years penal servitude, Portland. Free pardon later.
- **Mrs. Everett**: widow, about 45, snow-white hair, dark piercing eyes. Obsessed with proving son innocent. Lodges at Red Doe.
- **Mrs. Fanny Armitage**: Hetty's aunt. Family cook line (Perrys). Swears Hetty to secrecy on Testament.
- **John Armitage**: uncle, innkeeper.
- **George Vincent**: Hetty's husband, farmer at The Gables, big rough man, jealous, dialect speech. Married 5 years.
- **Dr. Arthur Rumsey, M.D., F.R.C.S.**: Harley Street, unmarried, brain/nerve specialist. Margaret's cousin.
- **Ann** (later Mrs. Henessey), **Dorothy**: Awdrey's sisters.
- **Sir John Cuthbert / Squire Cuthbert, Lady Cuthbert**: Cuthbertstown; Mr. Cuthbert a magistrate.
- **Awdrey's father**: magistrate, matter-of-fact; died 4 years after wedding.
- **Jim**: old prize-fighter who taught Awdrey "prod him in the mouth".
- **Hawkins**: butler at Court. **Mrs. Burnett**: housekeeper. **Davies**: groom. **Griffiths**: steward. **Dr. Cowley**: specialist. **Susan**: dairy maid. **Dan**: farm man. **Rover**: dog. **Johnson**: bailiff.
- **Little Arthur**: son, ~4 years old, dies of double pneumonia.

## Background
- Awdrey family "doom": West Indian heiress ancestor (150+ yrs ago) brought curse. Men suffer lapse of memory for grave events, retain minor ones; lassitude, moral decay; idiocy or death before 30. Girls spared.
- Awdrey's father had a Scotch wife, believed curse broken.

## Chapter Events (in order)
**I.** Evening, Red Doe Inn, ivy/honeysuckle. Everett and Frere on porch. Hetty appears. Frere jealous; Hetty tells Everett "Hetty" was allowed. Hetty gives Everett honeysuckle buttonhole, Frere heart's-ease ("There's meaning in heart's-ease"). Frere says Hetty proposed that morning. Hetty teases. Aunt Fanny objects. Hetty dreams of Awdrey; reads L.E.L. poems by brook. Awdrey: "Good-evening, Mr. Robert." Message: Squire wants uncle at Court. Frere forces kiss; Awdrey "Hold, sir!", leaps brook, "I will see you home." Frere: "I am going to marry Miss Armitage." Hetty denies it.

**II.** Family curse history. Awdrey's warning to Frere ("Her uncle is one of my father's tenants"). Frere: "I'll have this thing out with Hetty." Frere to Hetty: "choose between that fellow and me." Hetty: "it's the Squire."

**III.** Everett leaves Armitage's latchkey. Frere runs onto Salisbury Plain. Recalls childhood knife attack on brother. Labourer: "There be some-un calling yer." Frere falls into hole; meets Awdrey in dark. Frere accuses Awdrey of wanting Hetty. Frere raises cane; Awdrey thrusts stick into Frere's right eye. Frere dead. Awdrey checks pulse, lights matches, sees blood on ferrule. Hides stick in alder/underwood copse. Home at midnight (stable clock). Finds note from Ann: picnic tomorrow at 2 with Cuthberts, Margaret. Sleeps.

**IV.** Picnic on plain. Awdrey tells Margaret of murder; Everett arrested; coroner's inquest. Margaret pale, weeps. Walks into copse. Awdrey proposes on one knee; Margaret accepts ("I will be your wife"). Asks engagement kept secret until murder day passes.

**V.** Cuthbertstown supper; Lady Cuthbert kisses Margaret. Awdrey walks home, thinks of Everett and Hetty. Hetty waits by hedge: will "be true" to him. Confesses she followed Frere, saw fight, claims Everett did it, killer went "in the direction of the town." Awdrey tells her to tell his father. Ann asks about meeting Frere; Awdrey claims he went to bed early (Ann says he said he was dead beat and pushed Margaret's note under door). Awdrey: numbness in back of head.

**VI.** Hetty's thoughts: she saw Awdrey kill Frere; Everett innocent but arrested; she will protect Awdrey. Mrs. Armitage scolds about ruin; Hetty finds corpse in parlour, shrieks. Hetty begs aunt in bedroom; "I saw the murder committed... It wasn't Mr. Everett... the man who killed Mr. Frere was Mr. Awdrey."

**VII.** Aunt makes Hetty swear on Testament ("I, Hetty Armitage, saw Mr. Robert Awdrey kill Mr. Horace Frere..."). Aunt swears to never tell. Aunt describes family curse and Perry family cooking for Court. Walking-stick has silver plate with name. Hetty and aunt sneak out window; plan to weight stick and sink in pond half a mile away.

**VIII.** Week: Awdrey's coming-of-age Monday; wedding Thursday the 24th; Everett trial Tue–Wed at Salisbury. Margaret asks postponement; Awdrey refuses; tells her about lost stick and numbness. Coming-of-age party; Awdrey dances with Hetty ("I'll give you a dance later"). Hetty asks if perjury is a sin; Awdrey: "It is perjury." Hetty goes home. Trial: Hetty testifies, faints after cross-examination. Verdict: Guilty, mercy recommended. Margaret collapses in Awdrey's arms: "eve of our wedding-day."

**IX.** Dr. Arthur Rumsey described; nerve/brain specialist. Five years pass. Awdrey and Margaret live in London (Seymour Street). Son Arthur born. Everett sentenced 14 years penal servitude. Margaret befriends Mrs. Everett. Awdrey's father dies; Awdrey dislikes Court. Awdrey now 26, grey hair. Rumsey's dinner party. Mrs. Everett asks Rumsey's help: "My boy is innocent."

**X.** Mrs. Everett visits Rumsey at 8am breakfast. Her account: she visited Grandcourt (stayed at Red Doe). Met Hetty on Plain (now Mrs. Vincent, farmer's wife, 3 miles off). Hetty fearful; says "I thank the good God that Mr. Robert is happy." Mrs. Everett says the other man was not Frank Everett. Hetty: "one was Horace Frere—the other was your son, Frank Everett," then flees. Rumsey thinks her nerves/drink; Mrs. Everett rejects his opinion.

**XI.** Margaret visits Rumsey. Describes Awdrey's symptoms: torpor, insomnia, nightly vision of murder ("globe of light," "picture"), "Ha, but he carries my stick." Last autumn at Grandcourt Awdrey roamed the Plain. Rumsey visits Awdrey at home (Moonlight Sonata played). Awdrey: "a wretched man," wants to end life. Rumsey takes him to his house.

**XII.** Awdrey admits family doom; Rumsey says the memory lapse is not serious. Rumsey gives Awdrey a bedroom, sits up. Night vision recurs: sees two men, one wearing his clothes.

**XIII.** Rumsey wakes him; champagne and meat. Awdrey recounts vision as Oxford undergraduates fighting over a girl, murder. Draws sketch (man with his back turned, stick in hand, Awdrey's build). Rumsey keeps the sketch.

**XIV.** Rumsey prescribes sea voyage (Cape), leave by Saturday. Awdrey meets Hetty in Green Park (in London). Hetty warns of Mrs. Everett, says Mrs. Everett visited Plain and heard the story. Awdrey notes his own "vision." Hetty: "Murder will out." Awdrey's son sickens after rainstorm; double pneumonia; Cowley consulted. Child dies ~6 a.m. after 24 hours, saying "'Ittle boy 'ove dad." Awdrey collapses, then forgets child existed.

**XV.** Awdrey denies ever having a child. Says he will go abroad; takes Margaret's £25 plus his own ~£15. Child's funeral. Mrs. Everett comforts Margaret. Awdrey returns, says he was searching for his stick. Rumsey tells him he had a son (shows photograph). Rumsey orders him to wear mourning and act as father. Awdrey decides to go to Court; Rumsey comes.

**XVI.** Arrive Grandcourt late; Hawkins greets them. Supper; Awdrey drinks champagne. Rumsey reads Treasure Island in yellow room, dozes. Awdrey wakes him; dreams of murder; walks to Plain and pond. Awdrey leans over pond; sees his own reflection; remembers he is the murderer. Says "I have seen the man's face." Recovered mentally, but moral sense not returned.

**XVII.** May. Farmer Vincent tells Hetty that Squire returns to live at Court and will stand for Grandcourt. Hetty takes laudanum from hidden bottle in dairy ("black medicine," "toothache cure" of aunt's). Vincent wants kisses; Hetty doesn't love him. Villagers greet Squire's carriage. Awdrey's eyes meet Hetty's; Hetty: "Aunt Fanny, he remembers!"

**XVIII.** Barn supper at Court. Hetty tries to reach Awdrey; faints in crowd; Awdrey takes her out. Hetty asks secret meeting; Awdrey: office, 6 o'clock tomorrow. Mrs. Everett confronts Hetty; Vincent intervenes ("Hetty ain't to say too strong"). Vincent suspects Hetty's secret; warns her "meet Squire at your peril."

**XIX.** Vincent's morning; Mrs. Everett meets him at field, offers £1,000 for the secret; he refuses. Mrs. Everett at Court breakfast; Awdrey and she face off. Awdrey leaves for office.

**XX.** Dairy: Susan, churn, laudanum-tainted cupboard, Susan notices. Vincent suspects Hetty; she gives him laudanum in stout. He sleeps. Hetty goes to meet Squire at 6.

**XXI.** Awdrey's inner conflict (conscience has woken). Decides his path; plans to silence Hetty and send her and Vincent to Canada. Office meeting: Hetty kneels, pleads silence. Awdrey asks about stick; Hetty says she and aunt threw it in deep pond. Awdrey: "God, Thy judgments are terrible."

**XXII.** Hetty walks home (up hill, pain in side). Finds Vincent dead on settle; dog Rover howls. Hetty faints.

**XXIII.** Awdrey alone in office; wrestles with devil/God; refuses dinner. Margaret comes, asks him home; he refuses. Rumsey arrives; Awdrey tells him he is "the possessor of a secret." Rumsey urges confession. Hetty enters; Awdrey: "Sit down... Rumsey, you had best leave us."

**XXIV.** Hetty recounts poisoning; burns laudanum bottle in range; goes to Squire on knees: "You must save me as I saved you." Awdrey decides to confess together with Hetty. They go to drawing-room: Margaret, Anne, Dorothy, Mr. Cuthbert, Rumsey, Mrs. Everett. Awdrey confesses murder of Frere before all. Margaret: "you have saved your soul alive." Hetty gives sworn deposition (recorded by Rumsey, signed). Mrs. Everett: "Little hypocrite—little spy!" Hetty collapses, dies of heart disease "accelerated by shock."

**Aftermath:** Everett pardoned by Home Secretary. Awdrey tried at Salisbury; Judge sympathetic; Rumsey testifies; verdict Not Guilty (self-defence, no intent). Mrs. Armitage corroborates Hetty's evidence. Final scene: Awdrey and Margaret in porch at Grandcourt. Awdrey: "a shadow over me." Margaret: "You can be a thousand times better... how a man may fall, rise again, and in the end conquer." THE END.
